findings.reproduction: POST /api/workflows/compile with "When a car enters Service Bay A with headlights on or off, create an alert" or "... headlights on and off ...". Also submit "Create an alert for 5 minutes a car stays in Service Bay A".
findings.expected: Reject competing states and ambiguous action/trigger boundaries; preserve complete intent.
findings.actual: Both competing-state requests return ok=true with a lights-on-only predicate. The undelimited action-first request returns dwell=300, donating the action duration to dwell. The residual filter strips unconsumed state words and ignores and/or.
findings.fix: Validate complete condition and clause spans. Reject leftover state/connective semantics and require an unambiguous action-first trigger boundary.

findings.reproduction: With max_concurrency=1 and overall=60 ms, delay actual getaddrinfo for the owned loopback destination by 500 ms and issue four sequential calls. Separately hold the admission lock for 130 ms and delay admit by 140 ms under overall=200 ms. Stall a real TCP TLS handshake with connect_timeout=40 ms and overall=500 ms.
findings.expected: Active underlying work retains capacity until termination. Admission and transport phases share one absolute deadline, and configured connection/TLS limits apply.
findings.actual: Four resolver helpers remain simultaneously active despite concurrency 1; permits are free after caller timeouts. All four later establish TCP connections, with zero POSTs. Admission takes 271 ms against 200 ms because it reuses the pre-lock remaining budget. TLS takes 511 ms despite the 40 ms connection limit.
findings.fix: Retain capacity until abandoned helpers terminate, or explicitly restrict validated private numeric-IP configuration and reject hostnames promptly. Recompute remaining time after waits and bound TLS by min(connect_timeout, remaining).

findings.reproduction: Send valid positive JSON over owned real TCP with conflicting duplicate Content-Length headers, an incomplete trailer ending "0\r\nX-QA: owned\r\n", or an invalid trailer. Exercise provider → router → persisted event → local notification. Additional malformed chunk-size/status/transfer-coding cases are recorded in extended_probe.py.
findings.expected: Ambiguous, malformed or incomplete HTTP framing never confirms a visual action; correctly framed controls succeed.
findings.actual: Eight extended malformed cases each produce visual_status=ok, action_status=done and one persisted Notification. Duplicate lengths overwrite each other; trailer processing accepts the first CRLF without requiring a valid completed trailer section; empty/signed chunk sizes are accepted.
findings.fix: Reject ambiguous duplicate framing headers, validate supported transfer coding/status syntax and unsigned nonempty hexadecimal chunk sizes, and parse valid trailers through the final blank line before returning success.

findings.reproduction: Compile a supported 1.25-second dwell through HTTP. Execute the exact production applyDraft/createWorkflow closures with recorded setters/fetch, submit their payload to the real API, explicitly enable, and compare production event-engine behavior at 1.1 seconds.
findings.expected: Apply draft → Create → Enable preserves the validated decimal duration exactly.
findings.actual: The compiled 1.25-second duration becomes stored 1.0. The UI-derived rule emits at 1.1 seconds while the original draft does not. Supported 1.4 and 1.44 seconds also become 1.0; the 150-second control remains correct. Explicit approval remains intact.
findings.fix: Remove Math.round, preserve the exact floating-point duration, allow decimal form input and display sufficient precision while retaining separate approval.
